notes: §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR18: "When an overflow condition exists, the UNSTRING operation is terminated, the NOT ON OVERFLOW phrase, if specified, is ignored and control is transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement or, if the ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-1", and after imperative-statement-1 "control is transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement" unless it branches. EmitUnstring latches one overflow flag for both GR17 cases: a pointer below 1 or past the sender at initiation sets it and skips every transfer (the receiver loop is the else arm), and unexamined characters after the last receiving area set it after the transfers; StringEmitter.EmitOverflow then runs the ON OVERFLOW statements exactly when the flag is set and the NOT ON OVERFLOW statements only when it is not, so a NOT phrase alone is skipped on overflow and execution falls to the next statement. The 2023 addition (EC-OVERFLOW-UNSTRING) cannot fire at 85: EcEmitter.EmitOverflow writes nothing unless EnabledHere finds the condition's checking enabled, and >>TURN is refused at --std 85 (COBOL0900), so 1985's straight-to-the-end disposition is the only one reachable. Probed at --std 85: pointer 0 with both phrases runs ON OVERFLOW with receivers, pointer and tally untouched; pointer 8 on a 7-character sender with NOT ON OVERFLOW alone runs neither and continues; pointer 7 (in range, last character) is not overflow; overflow with no phrase continues with the receivers filled, the pointer at 7 and the tally at 2; ON OVERFLOW GO TO leaves the statement to the named paragraph; a multi-statement imperative with an IF ... END-IF runs whole and control then passes to the statement after END-UNSTRING. The witness is the second GR17 case with both phrases: ON OVERFLOW runs, NOT ON OVERFLOW does not, and the next statement follows.

next.reason: 1985: on overflow 'the UNSTRING operation is terminated, the NOT ON OVERFLOW phrase ... is ignored and control is transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement or, if the ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-1'. §2023:14.9.48.4 GR16 keeps termination, ON OVERFLOW and ignoring NOT ON OVERFLOW, but adds 'The EC-OVERFLOW-UNSTRING exception condition is set to exist' and, without ON OVERFLOW, 'execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.4, Nonfatal exception conditions': with checking enabled a PERFORM WHEN phrase (§2023:14.6.13.1.4 GR2) or an applicable USE declarative (§2023:14.6.13.1.4 GR3) runs before execution continues (§2023:14.6.13.1.4 GR4). The overflow now raises an exception condition and can divert control, where 1985 always went straight to the end of the statement.
